notes.title: Crusader: DE - Update & DLC 1 Reveals
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Yn98HHTPl4k
With your help [b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] has charged into the breach and emerged from its launch victorious! The response from fans has been nothing short of stellar and we're pleased to reveal some of our initial content plans in today's developer update!

While we're still working hard to add features, fixes and tweaks that players have been requesting (See our extensive [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3024040?emclan=103582791474973564&emgid=510713456384540934]v1.03 Patch Notes[/url] for the latest changes), we're keeping this momentum going by revealing new details of gameplay content players can look forward to in the coming months. With additional updates like v1.03 and more coming before then...

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/7e913c19b867710e01e146ce956448016cbc3536.png[/img]

Our first major ‘Autumn’ update will arrive in two parts, a free content update and an optional paid DLC. This will introduce The Crocodile, a brand new computer-controlled opponent with his own tactics, castle design, army and of course, snappy personality!

A wizened lord of the marshes, The Crocodile is a bitter cruel fellow, driven beyond sanity by envy of his rival lords. Players will encounter The Crocodile across a new five mission economic campaign, in addition to being playable in skirmish mode (And in case you’re wondering - Yes, the campaign has actual crocodiles too!)

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/7557f64cf23973225f79db991c093f05eb189374.png[/img]

While there will be some degree of combat to contend with in the economic campaign, the ultimate goal and thus victory will be decided by mastery of the game’s various economic industries and castle-life mechanics. The free component of the Autumn Update will be capped off by the inclusion of three new maps - One for Skirmish, Freebuild and Multiplayer.

These will release alongside our first DLC featuring two new CPU commanders in the form of The Canary and The Trader, as well as a new 9 mission ‘Sands of Time’ skirmish trail. Players can expect military scenarios will test their strategic prowess and skills of siegecraft, as they wage war against these new tricky CPU characters. Fear not, more about these new adversaries and their attributes will be revealed in due time!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/59e21472a7555da6a8e316f878fe973f43fe3f13.png[/img]

After Crusader: DE’s fantastic launch, we are determined to keep pushing further with fixes, content updates and gameplay improvements inbound, to truly make this Definitive Edition a game worthy of the Crusader name.

Thanks for playing and stay tuned for more updates coming soon!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

notes.title: Stronghold Crusader: DE - Roadmap Reveal
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=71UzpnLOH7U

[h1]Updates and DLC To Add New Lords, Customisation and More![/h1]

Good Day, Sire! [b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] is now less than two weeks from launch, so what better time than now to share all there is to know about the game's post-release plans!

Following the positive reception of the two public demos and in keeping with Stronghold: DE’s post-launch, we're announcing two major post-launch content updates for Crusader: DE. These will take the form of an Autumn and a Winter Update, both releasing this year alongside two paid DLCs.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/8f40990ce7a71421b643639197584c99a4027f26.png[/img]

The free initial Autumn Update will feature a series-first economic campaign as well as a brand new CPU commander. Five missions will challenge players to complete a series of economic objectives, leaning heavily into our city builder gameplay mechanics. The new computer-controlled character can meanwhile also be played as friend or foe, selectable in the game’s offline skirmish and online multiplayer modes. Last but not least, three new maps will also be added, one for skirmish, another in Free Build mode and a balanced multiplayer battlefield.

Following this content drop, the game’s free Winter Update will add perhaps the greatest player request so far... The ability to customise CPU opponents, castles and campaigns! Players will be able to create the rivals or allies of their dreams (or nightmares), design their defences and then place all of this into custom mission scenarios created by the community.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/32942208/5313cab036a111f6c5b495987e9b8564aad4fdd7.png[/img]

If that wasn’t enough, the Winter Update continues this community-first trend with the addition of a second co-op trail of missions. The 10 missions found in the first co-op trail not enough for you? Well, dare to brave the challenges of this new trail and you just might come out victorious. Once again a new map pack of three maps will be added to the overall pool, keeping things fresh for players after launch.

[b]Stronghold Crusader: Definitive Edition[/b] launches soon on July 15th. Wishlist now to be the first to know when it goes live!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3024040/Stronghold_Crusader_Definitive_Edition/

notes.content:
[previewyoutube=G83sagx-Tds;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Snarls[/b] Soon you will see what it means to wage real warfare! That is... In our final instalment of the [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] 'Jewel' campaign! [i]Valley of the Wolf[/i] extends the base game with seven new missions and extra achievements. Under the tutelage of the wise Sergeant, finish the fight by rescuing Sir Longarm's captured kin once and for all, when this new DLC releases for $2.99, €2.99 and £2.49 on April 30th.

This final chapter of 'The Jewel' campaign pits players against the greatest rogue of them all... The vicious Wolf! To safely retrieve the Jewel of the North and put an end to The Wolf's insidious scourge, players must plunge directly into the belly of the beast and bring the fight to his borders. notes.title: New Dev Diaries & Gameplay
notes.content:
[h1]Increased Troop Limits, Rally Points and Free Build Improvements![/h1]

[h2]Developer Diary - Episode 2[/h2]
[previewyoutube=ZVyWb3tqtds;full][/previewyoutube]

In our second [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] dev diary we discuss the genesis of the game, while delving into changes made as part of this new edition. Join Stronghold series veterans Simon and Paul, as they provide insight into the creation of our latest game from their unique perspectives.

We discuss the aims of Stronghold: DE and goals for everything from new single player content, all the way down to the smallest quality of life enhancements. Starting with the initial project pitch, then leading to questions of the scale of changes and finer elements like the actual difficulty of the new content, the road to release has been carefully considered.

It also gives us great pleasure in this video to confirm some of these changes and a few entirely new ones! In response to player feedback we have increased troop and building limits across all game modes, allowing for up to 3000 units and 2000 buildings at a time. By doubling these limits from the original game, we hope to provide you with more epic Stronghold sieges than ever before.

[h2]Developer Diary - Episode 3[/h2]
[previewyoutube=Y6dqDSJov1w;full][/previewyoutube]

We then round off our trio of behind-the-scenes videos by adding production expert Dave to the mix! It's time to talk Steam multiplayer, Workshop and the other improvements coming to your favourite game modes. What to expect from Workshop support, more details on multiplayer in DE and planned improvements to Free Build mode are all touched on, with extra insight into the development process of this unique game.

Making Stronghold more accessible has always been a key goal of the Definitive Edition and bringing our amazing multiplayer community - as well as the awesome maps they've created over the course of two decades - front and centre within Steam is how we're hoping to accomplish that. Thousands of fan creations can soon exist within Steam Workshop and be easily accessible for future generations of Stronghold players, with an improved set of multiplayer options to support years of continued play.

Add to this a few choice improvements to Free Build - everyone's favourite cozy game mode - and you have plenty to look forward to come release. In the meantime please check out our recent Free Build Q&A and Campaign Gameplay videos, where we confirm new features like Rally Points and discuss the series' 20 year legacy:

[h2]Free Build Q&A[/h2]
[previewyoutube=o2vMq9z_Dik;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Campaign Gameplay[/h2]
[previewyoutube=N5MIqMtuFkA;full][/previewyoutube]

Stay tuned for more updates between now and release as we process all your valuable feedback and incorporate as many changes as we can before launch. Thank you once again for your continued support and we hope you join us on November 7th by wishlisting the game on Steam!

Castle builders and fans of feudal taxation rejoice! As part of [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zQLCg46Q8nY]Steam Next Fest: October Edition[/url] and in celebration of almost 200,000 wishlists, we have just released a brand new [i]Stronghold: Definitive Edition[/i] demo - Our final playable build before launch!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2140020/Stronghold_Definitive_Edition/

Available exclusively on Steam as part of Next Fest, this demo features never-before-seen-missions - including your first look at our brand new single player campaign. This includes Missions 3 and 8 from the original 2001 [i]Stronghold[/i] military campaign, as well as a challenging mission from the exclusive new Definitive Edition campaign. Need a refresher? We encourage you to download the demo and leave us feedback! As with our previous demo there is a feedback form embedded in the game's main menu. So please build, besiege and let us know what you think.

notes.title: Skirmish Trail Update
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dWki5r4ohZs
We have now released version 1.4 of [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] on Steam! The Skirmish Trail Update introduces Warlords' first ‘skirmish trail’, a series of challenging missions with unique conditions to overcome and achieve victory. Other features added in the update include a new mounted soldier, two additional AI warlords, the return of a popular building for healing units and two extra multiplayer maps.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/ae5c43c32ebeaa05c51b7f70969eb29297e9504f.png[/img]

A classic mode introduced in the original [b]Stronghold: Crusader[/b], skirmish trails invite experienced players to display their mastery over Stronghold’s economic gameplay and RTS combat. Each trail mission pits player lords against a unique combination of AI opponents, recruitable warlords, resources, starting goods and teammates across a combination of new and existing maps. Choosing between ‘Standard’ and ‘Challenging’ difficulties, the classic ‘Chicken’ feature can also be used to skip missions players find too difficult.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/ec31d6f0eaa09942a03d08c2bd55aaae008c2224.jpg[/img]

The mounted Samurai Lancer marks Warlords’ first post-release unit, boosting the game’s launch roster of 16 soldiers and 10 siege weapons. With the ability to buff attack damage for all nearby mounted allies, the Samurai Lancer is a powerful new Japanese unit type. Armed with a piercing lance and clad in samurai armour, the Lancers are based on the Onna-musha female warriors of pre-modern Japan. Highly-skilled horsewomen as fast as Auxiliary Cavalry, but with an attacking strength comparable to their Imperial brethren, the Samurai Lancer provides support for other mounted units while also packing a punch of their own.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/6cd460e4356f913b621816ada52ca013cb6ccc67.jpg[/img]

A common request pre-release and one built into Warlords’ content roadmap from an early stage, the ability to heal units is now available in the new Field Hospital structure. A unique building that can be placed by any Beetle Warlord under your control, the Field Hospital heals all allied troops standing within its area of effect. Upgrading the Beetle Warlord will also increase the amount of healing given to troops over time, making this Edict even more effective at protecting defensive troops or those stationed in preparation for a siege.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/1ff63f3c095d5b948d60f151ad9a52431fea61d5.jpg[/img]

The Beetle and Bear Warlords are the first of several new warlords being added to the game in 2021. In addition to the aforementioned Field Hospital, the Beetle Warlord is a master of defence, giving players access to cheaper castle traps and shipments of armour. The Bear Warlord meanwhile is all about strength in numbers, improving the buff radius of Imperial Bannermen and making Imperial troops more affordable. The Bear is also effective for feeding your population and can even launch siege attacks of his own!

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/f72ba1394473803037bd8a6eca03054f665294a7.jpg[/img]

Finally both the Ascendance and Guarded Crossings maps are now available for use in skirmish mode and online multiplayer. Ascendance is a large four player map that proves some lords are more equal than others, giving each a chance to secure the high ground and claim victory. Meanwhile Guarded Crossings sees the northern player benefit from a large build area, but without access to the valuable warlords their rivals will be hotly contesting.

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/d4ba6aa811c00d0e00843dc2e8e6733994fca277.jpg[/img]

While the release of the Skirmish Trail Update and version 1.4 brings us to the end of our initial spring/summer content roadmap, rest assured more updates are on the way! This will begin with the reveal of our summer/autumn roadmap, with full details on that arriving next month. So if you're hungry for more [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] content be sure to keep an eye on our official Discord server and YouTube channel for the latest updates.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/907650/Stronghold_Warlords/

Today [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b] gets its first major content release with the Sun Tzu v1.2 Update! Adding requested features such as a new AI opponent, AI invasions in Free Build mode, a new Free Build map, general fixes and AI improvements, this update is now available to all players.

Initial testing puts Sun Tzu at the higher end of the difficulty scale, particularly when combined with the newer Extreme difficulty option and other tweaks possible in skirmish mode. [img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32942208/110cd2423592a5714c8ef47e121d47be83b98500.jpg[/img]

Now not only can you build to your heart's content in Free Build mode, but also use this time to prepare for war! notes.title: The Soldiers of Warlords #4
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oQQ3lk3enKM
We have released new gameplay footage revealing four brand new units coming to our upcoming ‘castle sim’ RTS [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b]. Each with their own special abilities, counters and tactics, the Ninja, Warrior Monk and mounted cavalry all make their Stronghold series debut in this new video.

The Ninja, Warrior Monk, Imperial and Auxiliary Cavalry join the game’s roster of 16 units and 10 siege weapons accessible to all players in skirmish mode and multiplayer. With more special and mounted units than ever before, [b]Stronghold: Warlords’[/b] new units aim to mix up the core series gameplay for long-time fans and newcomers alike.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/b86d420fa525234e65e738635d5794543ac0980c.jpg[/img]

[h3]Ninja[/h3]
Heavily reliant on remaining undetected, the Ninja is all about espionage. Able to deal high damage at range using her shuriken attack, in addition to classic invisibility and wall scaling abilities, Ninjas are more ‘hit and run’ than Assassins from previous Strongholds. When micromanaged or used in small squads, Ninjas are a force to be reckoned with. More than capable of taking out several high priority enemy units in quick succession, players will need to remain vigilant to avoid death by ninjitsu.

[h3]Warrior Monk[/h3]
A well-rounded soldier with specific battlefield applications, the Warrior Monk is a finely honed living weapon. Lightly armoured and fast on his feet, this unit is capable of dealing high damage quickly and is purpose made for surprise attacks. When surrounded by three or more enemy units the Warrior Monk’s spin attack will be triggered, knocking nearby enemies out of range while also dealing damage. Built for rushing enemy forces and repelling rival special units like the Imperial Guardsman, the Warrior Monk is excellent for quickly changing the ebb and flow of a battle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/bb2af0985df5be159b49d39b821a9082f1d86697.jpg[/img]

[h3]Imperial Cavalry[/h3]
The Imperial Cavalry’s high damage output and heavy armour makes them likely candidates for last horses standing. As such they are more suited to breaking enemy lines than their Auxiliary counterpart and serve a different function on the battlefield. Their charge ability can also be used to catch enemies off balance, quickly flank them or simply charge formations head on to weaken and displace their front line.

[h3]Auxiliary Cavalry[/h3]
Faster moving than their heavily armoured Imperial counterparts, Auxiliary Cavalry are the bread and butter of a mounted attack. These faster mounted units are equipped with light armour, a shield and lance.  Able to quickly react and change course, Auxiliary Cavalry are designed to take the worst of the enemy’s defences and allow your more powerful units to plough through.

notes.title: The Siege Weapons of Warlords
notes.content:
[h1]Fire Ox, Laddermen, Mantlets & Catapults![/h1]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DujbdkMBuUI
From the moment we deployed that very first Trebuchet nearly 20 years ago to today's rampaging Fire Ox in [b]Stronghold: Warlords[/b], our castle sim series has a long history of siege warfare. So assemble your Laddermen and load up your Catapults, because today we bring you our first episode in a brand new series called ‘The Siege Engines of Stronghold’. We're kicking things off with a mixture of classic fan favourite castle conquerors and brand new tower topplers, diving in with humble Laddermen, trusty Mantlets, classic Catapults and chaotic Fire Oxen! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/186136e5505a6f581d72cbdf44a81933fa66f371.jpg[/img]

Based on the historical sieges of ancient China, ranging from Tian Dan’s 3rd century BC assault on the city of Jimo through to the Siege of De’an in 1132 AD, the Fire Ox has an interesting history. With incendiary fabrics attached to its tail and spears at its side, this living weapon was an unexpected force to be reckoned with. Capable of decimating enemy siege lines before they knew what hit them, the Fire Ox was an unorthodox but effective tactical solution to a common siege scenario. Alongside series classics like the Mantlet, Laddermen and Catapult, the Fire Ox rounds out this first set of siege weapons to be revealed for the latest entry in our series.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35216938/406609552a1d417d8903af18370c7d3bc85f3d84.jpg[/img]

Players will be able to use virtual gunpowder in their castle defences, economy buildings and siege weapons, which will all use this new resource type in different ways. Fire Oxen, Fire Lancers, gunpowder traps and more will build on the series’ love of fire to give players completely new options for blowing apart rival castles in story mode, skirmish or online against friends. As Nick announces in the video, this is merely the first of several episodes in our new Siege Engines mini-series. So make sure you Wishlist for future instalments covering the revered Trebuchet and more!

[h1]Lead Coder Talks Stronghold @ PAX East[/h1]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1myBHEh60v8
Our second major update on the Stronghold front comes from the game's Lead Programmer himself! While at PAX East showing players our new tactical dungeon crawler [i]MetaMorph: Dungeon Creatures[/i], we sit down with Tony to discuss the upcoming game's setting, returning features, overall gameplay and direction.

To tide everyone over until our next feature and the full gameplay reveal later this year, this interview covers a number of points of interest for series fans:
[list]
    [*][b]Sequel?[/b] - Tony confirms that Stronghold Next will be neither Stronghold Crusader 3 nor Legends 2. These games could still happen, but we have no plans at this time.
    [*][b]Returning Features[/b] - In addition to confirming skirmish for the game, our new interview sheds light on a few classic features and units returning for this brand new Stronghold.

[/list]

Our upcoming Stronghold will be self-published by Firefly Studios on Steam and released when it's ready. In addition to Next being a completely new entry in the series another top priority is to deliver a fun, polished game from day one that incorporates as many fan-favourite features and touches as possible.

[h1]Brazilian Portuguese Now Available![/h1]

For the first time ever our updated HD version of the original [i]Stronghold[/i] (2001) is now available with full BR-PT language support:

[list][*]On-screen text, subtitles and sound.
[*]Over 1000 lines of spoken dialogue and 1.5 hours of new audio.
[*]Hear your favorite characters insult you in your native tongue!
[*]A first for Stronghold HD.[/list]

As with the release of the original HD update in late 2012, this new language is free for all existing owners of the game. To change the game language for Stronghold HD on Steam please follow these instructions:

[olist][*]Log into your Steam account.
[*]Right click on a game from the Steam game library and choose Properties.
[*]Go to the Language tab.
[*]Select the language you wish to use from the drop-down menu.
[*]Click OK.[/olist]

[b]Please Note[/b] - Files for this language may need to be downloaded before you can play.
